summary: For a focused Okanagan service website, CAD $3,000 to $4,000 is a practical planning budget when content, page count and integrations are controlled; Michael McKerracher's full website packages start at CAD $2,500. Compare quotes by design, copy, mobile enquiry flow, search setup, ownership and launch support. Confirm hosting, maintenance and future changes separately so the price describes the complete arrangement you are buying.
takeaways: A planning budget is not a complete project specification.
Compare the same deliverables across every quote.
Separate the build from hosting, maintenance and ongoing marketing.

sections.body:
Look at exactly which pages, audiences and actions a quote covers before comparing prices. A focused service site with a simple enquiry form is a very different build from an online shop or a booking system that handles staff schedules and payments.

What changes the scope of a website
BuildMain workQuestions to settle
Focused service websiteService pages, proof and enquiry routeWho writes the content and handles enquiries?
Booking websiteAvailability, services, confirmations and integrationsIs the booking system already chosen?
Online storeProduct setup, checkout and ordersWho supplies product data and manages fulfilment?

With a planning budget of CAD $3,000 to $4,000, I usually recommend putting the core service website first and pricing substantial integrations on their own. My web design work is quoted against an agreed scope rather than being offered as one fixed package for every business.

Content is genuine project work, so check whether the quote includes interviewing you, planning the page structure, writing the copy, preparing FAQs and turning past projects into convincing evidence.

If you are supplying the words and images, agree the format and delivery date upfront. If they need to be created, that work belongs in the initial price. Five pages could mean five blank layouts waiting for your material, or five finished pages with research, writing and approved imagery. Those are very different things.

Treat original brand photography and video separately from general image selection when that makes sense. Custom imagery can make a website more persuasive, but the production effort should be clear in the quote.

Compare the service information and enquiry routes in my selected website work with the pages your own customers need. A portfolio is most useful when you can see how the designer handles a real business problem.

Ask what is actually being designed and how feedback will work. Are you choosing an existing theme, adapting a design system, or commissioning a visual direction that is built around your business?

Look past the homepage and ask for examples of service pages, forms and mobile layouts. A proper design system covers headings, spacing, colours, buttons, images and repeatable content patterns, because that is what lets the website grow consistently.

Find out how many review stages are included and what counts as a change of scope. Agree who signs off the direction before the full build starts, because foundational decisions made too late lead to expensive revisions.

Check which search work is actually included at launch. Useful foundations are page planning, titles, headings, internal links, crawlability, sitemap setup and redirects where existing URLs change.

Ongoing SEO is separate: finding new content opportunities, improving existing pages, maintaining business information and measuring the results. If a provider promises an SEO website, ask what specific tasks that means.

Find out which accounts you will control and how results will be reported. Search Console impressions, website enquiries and booked work are all different measures, and a report should explain the connection without pretending every visitor is a prospective customer.

An integration costs more than adding a button when it needs to pass data between systems. Ask which booking tool, CRM, payment system or email platform is involved, and who is supplying access.

Test what happens after the user clicks. Does the correct service carry through? Is the booking confirmed? Where does the enquiry appear? Who deals with errors? Linking to an existing booking platform is a very different scope from custom scheduling or automated follow-up.

Ask for recurring software charges to be listed separately from the developer’s work, because that is what lets you compare the total cost of the arrangement rather than just the launch invoice.

Find out who controls the domain, hosting, content, design files and platform account. Ask what can be exported and what happens if you change providers later.

Decide whether you want to edit the site yourself, ask for occasional changes, or pay for ongoing support. Any training should cover the work you will actually be doing. A proper handover includes account access, editing instructions, form routing, renewal dates and a record of important integrations.

If you are comparing a monthly website offer with an upfront build, ask about minimum terms, cancellation, buyout and migration. The monthly number on its own does not tell you what you own.

Continuing costs can include domain renewal, hosting or platform fees, maintenance, content changes and optional marketing. Ask for an annual view of these costs next to the initial project price.

Published local offers show how much scope matters. On October 11, 2026, Svice listed a six-page package from CAD $2,820 with the client supplying text, logos and images, and one year of hosting included. Duford Digital listed template sites from CAD $2,025 and custom builds from CAD $5,940. These are individual offers with different terms, not an Okanagan market average.

Use a written checklist when you compare quotes: pages, content, design, search setup, integrations, ownership and continuing costs. If a provider cannot explain a line item, ask before you commit. A free initial conversation with me can help you turn your business objective into that brief.

faqs: Is CAD $3,000 to $4,000 enough for my website?

CAD $3,000 to $4,000 can be a practical budget for a focused service website with an agreed page list and a simple enquiry route. Decide who supplies the copy, photography and approvals before requesting quotes. Ask providers to price that same brief and list booking, payment or CRM integrations separately. Michael McKerracher’s full website packages start at CAD $2,500; the final price follows the agreed scope.
Are hosting and SEO included in a website build?

Only when the written quote includes them. Separate launch search work, such as headings, page titles, redirects and sitemap setup, from an ongoing SEO programme. For hosting and maintenance, record the account owner, renewal price, included updates and support arrangements. Svice’s published six-page offer includes one year of hosting; that does not establish the renewal cost or terms of another provider’s quote.
How can I reduce cost without weakening the website?

Start with the services and pages that help suitable customers enquire, then phase less urgent content and integrations. Supply organised, approved words and project photographs to reduce production work. Keep mobile usability, redirects, contact-delivery checks and account handover in scope. Agree a cost and approval process for later additions so a smaller launch does not become an open-ended project.
What does the free homepage preview include?

Michael's offer is a free custom homepage design preview with no obligation to hire him. It lets you assess a visual direction before agreeing to paid website work. A finished website is scoped separately, with full packages starting at CAD $2,500 and hosting, support and deliverables agreed before the build.
How do I compare ongoing website costs?

List hosting, platform subscriptions, domain renewal, paid integrations and maintenance for each proposal. Ask which updates are included and how new work is priced. Compare the same expected period and confirm exit and ownership terms so a low initial price does not hide costs or restrictions that matter later.
